title: Doors to Truth
text:
Instinct is the first door
Through which truth appears from the universal store
Memory is its tool
For survival our animal past has created a pool
It commands us to pull our hand from fire
And to run when danger is dire
There is no scope to reason
Spontaneously, the body works with precision
It captures the known
And springs out truth from the infallible zone
It is an inheritance of millions of years
From the unconscious mind like a flash it appears

The second door to truth is intellect
Through reason, truth it seeks to collect
This is a recent arrival
Truth here seeks to move beyond survival
Reason we need to acquire and cultivate
With logic, argument and proof it does cognate
Spontaneously it cannot function
It uses a process to reach a conclusion
Intellect is an effort to seek the unknown
But into intelligence it needs to be grown
Since reason always comes with doubt
Into wisdom it must transcend for intelligence to sprout

The third door to truth is intuition
From some unknowable source it is a revelation
It simply bubbles up as dream, vision or vibe
And reveals the deepest truths of human tribe
Without a vehicle it travels
Without any steps it ravels
It is an inner light
Without a source which burns bright
It is a leap
Into mysteries profound and deep
Here truth is revealed from beyond the mind
To the rarest of rare this ability is confined

Truth we wanted to discover
The secrets we wanted to uncover
So in the consciousness of man
The whole ladder when we ventured to scan
Three doors we found
With a sliding scale of truth they were bound
The door of instinct is open for all
While intuition remains an esoteric call
Intellect can act as a bridge between the two
And to explain the truth which by intuition we knew
Instinct belongs to the body and intellect to the mind
And only in depths of our soul intuition we can find

title: The Trial
text:
A great monk
With some unknown wine he was always drunk
He lived in the company of hills so high
And he could talk to the birds as they would fly

He became a beloved of the king and the masses
His appeal was beyond the classes
There was a rumour all around
And its whisper so profound

That he had come to know what truth was
The stuff with which you could make all the laws
Which was the source of the lasting glee
To all the secrets it was the key

One day when his country he decided to leave
Everybody started to mourn and grieve
When he was about to cross the border
He was arrested on royal order

With the greatest honour known to man
He was brought to the capital in royal caravan
The king and the queen came to the high gate
To welcome the prisoner so great

And he was requested to mount
On the seat paramount
The king himself sat on the floor with his kin
And ordered the trial to begin

“My Lord, this most venerable monk
With the wine of truth he is drunk
Everybody can smell
Yet he refuses to tell

The fact we want to expose
Is that he’s the only one who knows
And he’s the only one who can say
Still, with truth he was caught running away

The beloved of one and all
He was caught escaping through the great wall
He was bent upon leaving
Even as all of us were grieving”

In defence
Against this charge of a strange offence
The monk’s laughter filled the royal courtroom
With the fragrance of an unknown perfume

The king then announced
As the judgement was pronounced
“Our country won’t be the same without you
So, pray give us a clue

Before you leave please write a book
In which we could ever look
Where truth we could always find
O venerable monk, please be so kind”

As a royal guest
The monk wrote a book full of wisdom and jest
Covered in golden hue
It contained everything he knew

The monk was now free to leave
Even though the masses had continued to grieve
The king organised the farewell so grand
And accompanied him till the end of his land

The greatest book ever written
With truth it was smitten
Back in palace as the king read
The last passage said

“Before the ink dries
Away the truth flies
The written word is dead
Truth cannot be said”

title: A Piece of Truth
text:
The devil and his friend
Were walking on a street
At the street’s end
They saw a man who with joy was replete

They watched the man stoop
And reach to the ground
As something he did swoop
The friend asked the devil—“What has he found?”

“A piece of truth he did just pick”
“This is very bad business for you”
“Oh not at all, as I’ll now employ my old trick
And help him organise it through”

Truth becomes a creed
As soon as we try to organise
Its spirit starts to bleed
And the essence of it soon dies

Is law not an organisation
For justice which is formed
Then how the process of adjudication
Can with truth be informed?

title: Encountering a Fact
text:
A monk devoted to Buddhist precept
The rules for all his life he kept
Once he was walking at night
When the mist of darkness had defeated all light

To forget darkness he started to sing
Accidently he stepped on something
A squeaking sound spread amidst the dense fog
He knew he had stepped on an egg bearing frog

The monk lost all his calm
His being was filled with regret and alarm
In view of the Buddhist precept of not taking life
With guilt his spirit was rife

With a heavy heart he continued to walk
Reaching home he refused to eat and talk
He threw himself on the bed
And took an extra pillow to rest his restless head

Past midnight when he managed to sleep
In his dream hundreds of frogs started to leap
All the frogs demanded his life
Each holding the sharpest knife

At the crack of the dawn
When the darkness had gone
He raced to examine the ground
He had stepped on an overripe eggplant, he found

Uncertainty at once stopped
All the burden of wrong knowledge dropped
Does there exist an objective world?
This enquiry is vital for Zen to be unfurled

To encounter a fact
Without prejudice we must act
When all imagination falls
Truth then appears and enthralls

title: Precedent—Whether a Way to Truth
text:
We were in quest
So we searched in east and west
We looked all around
Truth was ultimately found

We marked the trail
To that holy grail
Where truth was resident
We called it precedent

But truth is not dead; it’s very much alive
To new places it likes to drive
Like universe it is ever growing
Like time it is ever flowing

It lives in the hobo style
Stays just for a while
Ever on the move
For long, it doesn’t like to groove

So precedent and its trail
With time are bound to fail
Again and again the way to truth must be found
With precedent it cannot be forever bound

The beaten track helps and aids
But it may not work always
When to truth it does not lead
New paths we may have to explore and tread

With truth alone our loyalty should lie
With old trails we need not always comply
If to truth a precedent blocks the way
Then that precedent we should be ready to slay

title: The Knight is Shy
text:
In the evening of his life
Tathagat had spoken incessantly for forty years
To thousands who came to end their strife
And to close forever their fears

To those who came from far and wide
To the kings and to the common folk
To the humble and to the ones full of pride
He continuously spoke

He was always surrounded by men so keen
One day, finding him alone Anand took him for a walk
In the garden green
When they began to talk

Anand so asked
“Bhante! You have been trying to help in every way
Your words have been beautiful and vast
And truth you have always tried to convey

But have you said everything and all
Or something still remains for you to expound”
It was the season of fall
And millions of leaves lay fallen all around

Tathagat stooped down to pick leaves a few
Which had turned grey
And as the winds blew
He began to say

“O Anand” looking at the leaves in his hand
“This is all I could say”
Then pointing to the millions scattered on land
“And all that I could not convey”

In silence truth is defined
We need to use our own light
And on our own we need to find
As shy is our knight

title: A Borrowed Light
text:
A master of Zen
Wise among men
Lived on a hill
With a mind so still

A disciple came to see
Both talked with glee
Time went by
There was now darkness in the sky

He forgot that he had to go
And cross the forest below
Dangerous was the passage to his home
Where wild animals did roam

It was already midnight
His face showed fright
The master asked him to start
“For your home you may now depart”

There was no light in the skies
And looking at danger in his eyes
The master gave him a light
“This candle will make your path bright”

The disciple was now sure
That the light will endure
Relieved and assured
His worry was now cured

As the disciple was about to start the long track
The master blew out and took his candle back
“Master, I don’t understand
How will I face the darkness so grand”

“Unto yourself be a light
Then your path will ever be bright
How far a borrowed light could go
For long the path it cannot show”

A truth that we borrow
Will fade today or tomorrow
If we know how to ignite
Our path will ever be bright

title: The Hue of the Strange Creature
text:
In a forest atop a tree
A strange creature was enjoying its insect-spree
As on the branches it started to tread
The news of the odd creature rapidly spread

Men full of surprise
Came to see the creature with their own eyes
As in the evening they met
They began to discuss the creature they could not forget
Its projectile tongue was long
And its grip was strong
It had a swaying gait
Alive the prey it ate
Its eyes could independently move
Waiting for the prey it would motionlessly groove

On its wonderful skills everyone agreed
But about its colour none could accede
One said its body is red
The other said green is all-over spread

Yellow was the third one’s view
To the fourth it was surely blue
The dispute was on its hue
The opinions were more than a few

This led to an argument aggressive
About one’s view each was possessive
So, they decided to visit the tree
In order to test their plea
Alas! the strange animal was not there
But a monk sat nearby engrossed in his prayer

“Sire, on this tree we have seen an animal queer
About its colour we would like to hear”
As before the monk the men bowed
It was the hermit who laughed out loud

“Sometimes it is red and sometimes green
And at times no colour can be seen
Sometimes it is yellow and sometimes grey
It can change colour at will to trick its prey”

Truth is one but many are its shades
When we see it, away the false fades
By argument alone we can’t prove
Only by experience our doubts we may remove
We need to see the spectrum whole
Only then it would descend to our soul

title: The Boy and the Fish
text:
The boy so young
With a question he was stung
With curiosity he did glow
About truth—he wanted to know

Straight he went to his mother
Who was cooking for him and his brother
“I am rather busy preparing a feast
Go and ask the wise old priest”

To the priest the boy then went
“Please tell Sir, by truth what is meant?”
“See, I am eating my dainty dish
Why don’t you go and ask the fish”

To the pond the boy then ran
Where the fish lived with her clan
“Fish O fish! Fish O fish!”
Fast the boy expressed his wish

“I will answer your question for sure
My boy, please worry no more”
As the fish assured the boy
He was instantly filled with joy

“But great thirst I feel
First fetch me a glass of water with zeal”
“What! What do you say?
Surrounded by water you ever stay”

“Oh! that’s what I mean”
The fish said to the boy so very keen
“Surrounded by truth you ever live
And to yourself only you may give”

title: Spectacles
text:
A long long time ago
God came to the Earth below
To live amongst people for a few days
So that He could witness the human ways
Men and women soon complained to Him
That their vision was dim

Some could not see far
They could hardly relish the twinkling star
Some could not recognise objects near
And to others with distortion things would appear
Miserable for their own malady
They all pleaded for a remedy

God took pity at their plight
And promised to help improve their sight
Back to His home when God went
To Earth His optician He immediately sent
The optician came with millions of glasses
Enough and more to satisfy the masses

From a wide variety people were asked to choose
Some were plain and others with colours did amuse
To pick spectacles of choice everyone was free
For coloured pairs there was a spree
For plain glasses the optician failed to persuade
As everyone liked to pick a different shade

Everyone profusely thanked God
For a gift that was much awed
Everyone now saw the world in a different hue
For the colours available were more than a few
Everyone was happy with his chosen pair
About others’ vision no one did care

Today as opinions these spectacles are known
Everyone feels that to him alone reality has been shown
Everyone feels that his outlook is true
Nobody is ready to accept other’s view
Everyone feels that his view is the best
And with truth he alone has been blessed

title: The Lost Axe
text:
When the axe of a nobleman was lost
Through his mind many thoughts crossed
He suspected a boy living in his own street
Whose behaviour was certainly that of a cheat

Just a week before
That boy had come to live next door
He said to himself, “when I first saw that boy
He looked just like a swindler and decoy”

A few days later while removing the hay sacks
The nobleman found his ‘stolen’ axe
In his own possession the axe had always been
That boy came out absolutely clean

Next day he saw that boy again
Nothing negative was processed by his brain
As a normal lad he did appear
A thief’s look he certainly did not bear

Like an active agent works an ordinary mind
Imaginary things it can always find
As a mirror it does not act
It has the capacity to distort a fact

It can easily colour reality
False it can readily invent and see
That boy remains the same
In-between the mind played many a game

Unless we remove the layer of illusion
We are liable to reach wrong conclusion
Truth can only be revealed
Off when all maya is peeled

title: Pebble
text:
Something new had dawned upon
In him a new truth was born
The world would not remain the same
And he would attain great fame

It was such a giant leap
The whole night he could not sleep
While thinking how to name this new-born
Night turned into dawn

He then decided to go for a walk
So that with the sea he could talk
While walking, a small pebble entered his shoe
Moist of the morning dew

As he stooped to remove the stone
Something emerged from the world of unknown
As the wind started to blow
Something he came to know

“On this tree so big
I sit on a very small twig
To the roar of this vast sea
I have offered only a small plea

In front of mysteries all
My knowledge is like this pebble so small”
Thus to name his discovery new
He got a cue

He decided to call it calculus
Even though his discovery was fabulous
To the world a great truth he had shown
But chose to call it a small stone

title: A Caravan in Search of Truth
text:
In the land of Hindustan
Six wise monks joined the great caravan
An unknown beast to see
Who had the secret of glee

Those six men were wiser than all
Most charming and tall
They were replete with grit and fun
Anyone they could outrun

Full of wisdom and pride
Their fame had spread far and wide
Though in argument they could defeat anyone
But they reached at night when light there was none

It was the turn of the first monk
Who touched the animal’s trunk
“It is a snake
Out I can easily make”

The second monk who touched the ear
“It’s just a fan, O men! my dear”
On the leg when the third one’s hand fell
“It’s a trunk of a great tree on which birds merrily dwell”

The fourth one reached to the side
“It’s a wall—strong and wide”
The fifth one picked on its tail
And described it as a rope in great detail

When tusk the sixth one felt
“It’s the finest spear in the battle to pelt”
Each propounded the secret of the beast
As if of truth he were the highest priest

Each one was right in his own way
But the whole truth remained still at bay
As people heard one of the greatest arguments known to man
Three more monks joined the great caravan

These three were equally wise
And they reached at dawn when they could use their eyes
But the first got drunk
And behaved like a spunk

The beauty of the beast made the second one silent
And he was no longer violent
When the beauty is so deep and dense
To say about it is nothing but an offence

The third one refused to tell
Howsoever you may plead and yell
“You must come to your own conclusion
Whatever I say will not take away your illusion”

This is the story of the great Indian Caravan
One of the greatest investigations into truth made by man
Many many thence came to join
But all of them can verily relate to these nine

title: Banish the False
text:
In the Kingdom of Travancore
When days were of the yore
Of truth the young king became a great fan
On falsehood he announced a ban

In his zeal, a new law he declared
Accordingly, falsehood was not to be spared
“Henceforth every liar would be put to death
The State will take away his breath”

Moral, the king wanted the kingdom to turn
Truth, he wanted everyone to learn
In unison all the wise men of the court agreed
“In our kingdom, only morality we should breed”

As the new law was announced in the crowd
It was the court fool who laughed out loud
In the presence of the king
The fool started to sing

“I am going to be hanged the next day
Come ye all to the gallows to slay
I have a desire to die
And thus I speak a lie”

Next morning everybody watched the fool
Who appeared at the gallows riding on his mule
“Pray hang me high
And with the new law please do comply”

When the fool challenged them to apply the law
The king noticed a flaw
As the fool continued to shout
The king shared his doubt

“If you hang him through
His words become true
If you do not hang
The new law falls on the ground with a bang”

The fool was indeed telling a lie
But it turns true if with the new law you comply
The fool so wise
Then merrily went back singing his advise

“Immorality who could banish
False would never vanish
Learn this truth so crude
Bring the law to human altitude”

title: Lawyer's Truth
text:
Two brothers lived together
Much wealth they did gather
But it was all through theft and deceit
One was a swindler and other was a cheat

From grace they did fall
Vices they had all
But of each other they were very fond
Of love there was an indelible bond

When one of them died
In grief the other one cried
Lest his brother’s memory should fade
A grand funeral he arrayed

But for service no priest was keen
As the brothers’ reputation was rotten and mean
Further he insisted that his brother be called a saint
Which proved to be the biggest constraint

Then he named a big sum
Still for service no one was ready to come
No one was willing to tell such a lie
As the dead man was a swindler and sly

At last a lawyer he approached
And the difficulty he broached
With professional oath the lawyer was bound
With truth his words must resound

But the sum named was such
And the temptation was so much
So, pandering to the greed
The lawyer agreed

The following day
Where the decorated coffin lay
The lawyer came down
Dressed in his gown

In front of the crowd
He started the service after he bowed
“The man you see in the coffin there
For him I do the prayer

He was a swindler to the core
And a rotter for sure
In the name of God I swear
No one did he ever spare

A villain, a delinquent and a culprit
There was hardly a crime that he did not commit
He had every possible taint
But in comparison to his brother he was a saint”

title: On the Road I Search
text:
With a home on the wheel
Deserts and mountains I want to feel
With a life on the move
I’m ever in the groove

Road is my only station
And journey the destination
To look at the stars for a while I stop
Then again I hop

The road is long
My friend, you’re welcome to come along
Together we’ll travel for a while
Then say goodbye with a smile

On the road I search
On the way I perch
Some unknown truth I seek
And on the road I find my peak

title: The Path
text:
“The path is not lit
A wrong trail I may hit
The journey is long
Pray come along

Darkness all around
Your presence so profound
From darkness to light
Take me to the path ever so bright”

“The path cannot be shown
The journey must be undertaken alone
Truth is beyond the print
And I can give just a hint”

When the path is ever so new
Catch the clue
A finger pointing to the moon
Is the greatest boon
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/KAOj-Cl-hlM

title: Justice—All too Human
text:
When we started living with others of our kind
The first law was born to help us bind
Cooperation was then the name of the game
But competition was the other side of the frame

It was natural for disputes to arise
‘Might’ was then the only device
Resolution was quick and on the spot
Fist was the way for justice to be sought

This justice gave us a woeful plight
But something in us it did ignite
Maybe might is not always right
And must we decide every dispute by a fight?

To decide who is right or wrong
Is there a need to show whose punch is strong?
Better use the spin of dice
And a toss of coin would be equally precise

Justice then became a game of ‘chance’
But fairness still could not advance
Again we wanted to revise
And searched for a man who was wise

Faith we must repose
And all argument we must close
When trust is in our heart
Only then the wise man would do his part

But faith in man does not abound
And ‘wisdom’ is so rare to be found
When the argument is wild and violent
Even the wise are forced to remain silent

In the present system ‘reason’ is all pervasive
But justice still remains elusive
Because reason we can always twist and turn
If winning is our only concern

A lawyer is ready with reason as his sword
Provided his fee we may afford
When might and chance also play their part
Modern justice becomes just a thing of craft

Overflowing now is our basket of litigation
And from vice there is no mitigation
Would we see light ever?
Or human justice is condemned forever?

Justice can have a human face
Only if two ideas we embrace
Choose those few who are just
And sue only when we must

title: Hide and Seek
text:
“Where do you hide?
With rules are you tied?
Where do you perch?
And how do I search?

To you I seek
Please do speak
I am in force
But in your name I wish to enforce

Where are you cast?”
The law so asked
Justice then replied
Merrily from her hide

“Sometimes between the lines
And at times out of the confines
Sometimes beneath the word
And at times away from the herd

Fix me in the letter
And I’ll defy the fetter
Where you most abound
There I’m rare to be found

I hate to settle
On the move I find my finest fettle
I follow no map and I carry no chart
So, seek me with all your heart

The more you seek
The more I attain to my peak
With you I like to play that ancient game
Hide and seek is its name”

title: Journey to the Mountain Top
text:
A poor farmer lived on the foot of a hill
Looking at the top he was always filled with thrill
The peak looked so beautiful from the ground below
But to the top he could never venture to go

The journey to the summit was long
And the Sun on top would be so strong
Necessary it was to complete the trip at night
Before the Sun would start to burn bright

On the way there was no place to camp
So, he bought himself a lamp
His desire he wanted to fulfil
With his lamp he began the voyage up the hill

Soon the Sun went down
And he could no longer see the hill and its crown
His lamp he then lighted
But still the hill and its top could not be sighted

The light of the lamp would go for only ten feet
With the hill and its top how could he then meet
The sad farmer sat on a rock
And down he broke

Now, there was no hope
He would never be able to reach the top
Just then an old monk passed by
He asked “Man, why do you cry”

When the farmer told his tale
The monk laughed like a mighty gale
“Madman, If you walk with your lamp
Ten feet ahead will always be under its stamp

This little lamp is worth
To take you to the whole earth
With a lamp in your hand
You may embark on a journey howsoever grand”

If you light the lamp of reason
It will work for every season
It is the master key
With which far you may see

When you walk with reason in your hand
You may travel to the farthest land
When justice lies on the mount so high
Reason alone will help you fly

title: A Lamp of Its Own
text:
We fix our eyes
On the footprints of the wise
We choose to tread
And allow our memory to lead
But the answers of the past
Forever cannot last
When the question is so new
Custom may not give us a cue

We look for advise
In the vision of the wise
On their imagination we rely
And choose to comply
But when in future the answers we lay
They may not always show us the way
When the question we could just not foresee
Legislation may not give us the key

Custom is wisdom forged through trials and strife
With speculations the legislation is always rife
In memory the custom always lies
In imagination the legislation always flies
In custom we always look back
In legislation we try to foresee the future track
But reality may be very different
So justice has to be a live current

To the past or future law belongs
But justice ever longs
For a tryst with the present
And to catch this very moment
Here and now it can only live
To the present alone it can give
Past or future it need not disown
But justice must have a lamp of its own

title: Bike and Balance
text:
Carbon it will not emit
And will also keep you fit
It may not have much of speed
But the planet will not bleed

As you rock and roll your knees
And feel the cool and lovely breeze
Wheels when you push and spin
Sure to be lean and thin

Pedal pedal off you go
Sometimes fast and sometimes slow
Pedal pedal up that hill
Then you slide back with thrill

Pedals in bike—there are two
Scales of law—the very same hue
Pedals move when you force
Law would work when you enforce

To keep the balance you must move
In the pedal you must groove
Still and stagnant law would fumble
Justice is then sure to crumble

Law and bike—both will fall
Balance if you fail to install
Balance in law when you keep
Justice you are sure to reap

title: The Colours of Law
text:
Beyond wrong and right
Between Black and white
The world of colours bright
Sure to convey delight

Beyond false and true
Between the extremes of two
With shades ever new
Joy we may construe

Beyond silence and plea
Between bound and free
In the tones of festive Holi
Let us find the glee

Beyond approval and protest
Between contract and contest
With the tints of fest
Let us create the jest

Beyond win and loss
Between criss and cross
The hues so gloss
Let us apply across

title: New Meanings
text:
Life brings trials new
Something we never knew
The old laws may not work
But beneath them new meanings do lurk

So, let’s look for a new thought
Something we had never sought
A whole new search
And a new branch to perch

So, let’s try a new trail
Though it has the risk to fail
But that brings in the thrill
And to test our will

So, let’s catch the new hint
Then new meanings we mint
The words may be old
But all their meanings have not been told

title: Eagle's Search
text:
A bird on the wing
Rocking like a king
Grace and glide
On the wing of pride

Playing all alone
With the winds unknown
Riding on the breeze
With utmost ease

Above the fog
Beyond the smog
He longs to fly
All doubts he seeks to defy

With skies he is bound
But eyes fixed on the ground
On the ground is his aim
It’s where lies the game

The law so regal
Learnt this secret from the mighty eagle
Only when high does he soar
The ground below he can easily explore

For truth can be found
Only amidst life on the ground
And when truth is in sight
Justice is then ever so bright

title: String and Kite
text:
“I want to fly
Take me to the sky
The song of life I long to sing”
The kite said to the string

But once it was high
String it wanted to defy
“Higher I want to go
Far I want to flow
You are holding my wing”
The kite told the string
With a heavy heart
The string decided to part

Soon the winds did betray
And the kite went astray
Though the kite was now free
But it was lost in the spree
Kite and string
Together they must cling
United they endure
Alone their fall is sure

Bereft of law, justice has no motion
Without justice, law loses locomotion
Separated they’re bound to fall
Only together they can respond to the call

title: Body and Soul
text:
The body is gross
But soul is the boss
Limited is the body’s role
It’s the vehicle of the soul

The body transforms to dust
Continually change it must
Soul is that which stays
Forever and always

The body a vessel of flesh and bone
While the soul has an ethereal tone
The body with its senses five
Joins with the soul and keeps alive

Together they make one whole
It’s not the body that dons the soul
Rather the soul wears a body
On the stage of life to embody

The body has a goal
To search for the soul
It’s a challenge to find
When subtle is its kind

Every law longs
To reach where it belongs
Justice is that sacred place
Where law comes to fruition and grace

title: Seed and Essence
text:
Filled with much information and pride
Shvetketu returns from the school of his guru and guide
But unable to answer the questions of his dad
He becomes so very sad

In order to hear that which can’t be heard
And to see when the vision is ever so blurred
The son then implores his dad
“Father, please teach me that which makes one glad”

“Pluck a fig
From the tree so big
Break it—and what do you see in all”
“Multitude of seeds extremely small”

“Break one seed and look inside
With your eyes open wide”
“Nothing I could discern
Howsoever I yearn”

“That which can’t be perceived
In that the fig tree is conceived
That subtle essence
Permeates the whole existence”

Gross is the body of law
But if we analyse it without flaw
Justice is what we find
Subtle alone is its kind

title: Paint and Painting
text:
Red yellow and blue
I shine in every hue
With emotion I do seethe
But I don’t yet breathe

I long to come to life
With beauty so much rife
Truth I wish to say
Joy alone I may convey

Need an artist with skill
Canvas who can fill
A painter who can paint
Without a single taint

The right fix does the magic
And even a slight lapse can make it tragic
Paint and painting—one or two?
It’s the application that holds the clue

A choice of right laws
An application without flaws
Created with hand, head and heart
Justice is indeed a work of art

title: Seed and Fragrance
text:
“With the stars I have a date
With the Sun I want to relate
I long to play with the air
My fragrance I want to share
Lonely I feel
To the earth I appeal
Take me in your fold”
The seed so told

“You need to dive inside the earth
To find out if you are worth
The rains will test
And the winds will attest
All challenges if you surpass
And every trial if you pass
We’ll see your flowers bloom
Your fragrance will then spread and zoom”

In the soil of dispute
The seed of law forms its root
When the light of reason showers
Law flowers
This flower carries seed and fragrance in twain
In seed, precedent we obtain
In fragrance, justice we attain
This cycle goes again and again

title: Word and Sense
text:
A great scholar he was
From all he received great applause
Naropa’s fame spread far and wide
And to thousands the monk was a master and guide

Always surrounded by scriptures—ancient and rare
With books alone he had an enduring affair
Once he had a vision of a hag—ugly and horrific
But in wisdom she was prolific

About books a dialogue between them did commence
She asked, “do you understand the word or the sense?”
Frankly, the monk replied “I understand the word”
Happy she became when this truth she heard

In truth all her ugliness started to submerge
And an ethereal beauty began to emerge
Wanting to make her more glad
“I understand the sense as well” the monk ventured to add

All her ugliness bounced back when she heard this lie
And she started to wail and cry
This vision of the woman so wise
Transformed the monk to realise

Knowledge of just the word
Bereft of sense is absurd
The woman was only a projection of the monk’s own soul
Thenceforth to know the sense became his only goal

Law is the word and justice its sense
Easy to cram law but knowledge of justice is often a pretence
To sense only rare do reach
And they alone should have the right to decide and preach

title: River and Ocean
text:
Wanting to explore the journey of the river to the ocean
The traveller consulted the scriptures with great devotion
The manuals differed in their account
About the river’s path as it flows from the mount

Then he consulted men who were wise
But varying was their advice
He then dropped all contradictions
And drew a map with just the common predictions

The long journey he did start
With the help of his chart
But the river did not adhere
The map it did not revere

By opinions the river was not bound
As its own wisdom was profound
To his logic the river did not aways conform
About change, it also did not inform

The river can only thrive
When its current is alive
The traveller soon realised, the river has not gone astray
Rather it’s the map that could not fathom the river’s way

A living law is subject to mutation
While justice remains its destination
To justice law may drive
Only when it remains fluid and alive

title: Sound and Echo
text:
A boy and his father went for a walk
Climbing the hill, they started to talk
“Ahhhh” the boy screamed, as he fell
In the same vein, the mountain did yell

With echo, the young boy had the first blush
“Who are you” was his spontaneous gush
“Who are you” prompt came the reply
It was like horror pouring from the sky

The boy then shouted “you are a coward”
And with the same words he was showered
Frightened, the boy asked his dad
“Who is this guy so very mad”

“Say something nice”
Was the father’s advice
“I love you” the son then shouted
The same emotion came back undoubted

“You are wonderful” the boy said with a smile
And received the reply in the same style
The boy was thrilled
With wonder he was filled

To his son full of surprise
Tells the father so very wise
“Whatever you send forth to the world
The same for you will be unfurled”

Law is like the sound
And for the echo of justice to be profound
Let us make law that is good, strong and kind
Only then true justice we shall find

title: Reality and Reflections
text:
Mirror palace it was called
Where mirrors of various kinds were installed
Thousands were there all around
On ceiling, walls and the ground

Wanting to explore
A little girl opened its door
Full of wonder and pride
She went inside

As she entered all alone
Thousands of images were at once shown
In some she was short and in others she was tall
At times she became big and then so very small

Some showed her fat
And other images were too flat
Bewildered she ran outside
Where she was comforted by the guide

With great affection
He explained the phenomenon of reflection
“To the mirror’s form
Your image must always conform”

Each mirror is like a unique set of facts
Different application it attracts
Law is the reality and justice its reflections
Reality is one but many are its projections

title: Finger and Moon
text:
A Zen teacher’s dog loved his evening romp
With his master full of play and pomp
The ball he would bound ahead to bring
Then back he would run
Wagging his tail with lots of fun
And then wait for the next fling

One evening the teacher invited his student
Of all he was the most prudent
An ardent scholar of the Buddhist way
But he was troubled by exceptions and conditions
Coupled with numerous contradictions
So to the teacher his difficulty he ventured to say

The teacher said waving his hand
“You must understand
In the golden way
Words can act only as guidepost
Truth in full splendour they can never host
Howsoever hard we may try to say”

The teacher then pointed to the moon
And asked his dog to fetch it soon
“Where is my dog looking”, the teacher enquired
“Only to your finger he does stare
Of moon he is not aware”
Answered the student who now looked inspired

The teacher who was wise among men
Then explained the art of Zen
“Don’t be like my dog
And if you don’t confuse truth with my finger
Then truth will never linger
Else it will be hidden ever in fog”

Law is just a hint
Of something that lies beyond the print
It is the finger that guides
But to the finger don’t cling
Rather, look at that luminous king
Beneath the clouds who hides

title: Bird and Bird
text:
A bird so small
Lived on a tree so big and tall
On the lowest branch, he had his nest
Of food, he was always in quest

One day when of chores he was free
He thought of exploring the tree
On the highest branch he saw another bird
But his sound he had never heard

With much verve
The second bird he continued to observe
Always calm and composed
He perceived the world with eyes fully closed

He looked so akin
As if he were his twin
With a burning desire to meet
He decided to go up and greet

But to the high branch he was a stranger
And the journey upwards was full of danger
Still he did start
With great hope in his heart

Branch by branch up he did move
His courage he had to prove
As he was just a bough away
In full splendour the second bird lay

Filled with joy and pride
He made the final stride
On top the sun was shining in full glare
But the other bird was not there

Are law and justice one or two?
Those birds give us a cue
Two in the beginning—like father and son
And finally merging into one

title: Stone and Stone
text:
The hill was tall
With a risk to fall
A challenge no small
But Sisyphus took up the call

Big was the stone
And the hill stood like a cone
He was all alone
And to dangers the journey was prone

He had to take the stone up that hill
Apart from labour it required skill
A test of his will
And a dream to fulfil

All the sweat to drain
He had also to face thunder and rain
But the human crane
Joyfully endured all the pain

Sometimes high and sometimes low
Sometimes fast and sometimes slow
But he never looked back and below
And further he continued to go

In the journey he did not whine
And when he reached the top he was on cloud nine
A feeling so divine
As if reaching a holy shrine

He did all the drill
Without a single shrill
But on top there was no place to rest and chill
And the stone started to roll down the hill

In the end, what did he attain?
Was there any gain?
Or did his effort go in vain?
The cycle goes over and over again

The stone was the law as it laid on the ground
With the hill of facts around
And when with the skill of Sisyphus it was bound
In the form of justice it was crowned

As the stone is back on the sliding course
And hits the ground below with force
Of law it again becomes a source
In another case for justice to enforce

title: Ten Travellers and a Monk
text:
Travellers they were ten
All brave and curious men
Bliss they all wanted to find
In forests and mountains they mined

They wandered with one aim
Bliss alone they sought to tame
At the end of one day
A stream came in their way

With flood she was gush
But they were in a rush
They decided to cross
Lest the night should come across

There was no one to deliver
They themselves had to cross the river
With courage they stepped in
The river they wanted to conquer and win

But the river was tough
And her flow was rough
Rocks blocked their path
While rain showed its wrath

At the close of the day
They were forced to return midway
Back on the bank they came
Forsaking their aim

Whether each one was back for sure
They wanted to ensure
As the moon started to mount
One of them began to count

When he could count only nine
It sent shivers down their spine
Then each one counted in turn
Now they were sure only nine did return

The whole night they wailed and cried
As one of them had probably died
Full of despair
They repented—why didn’t they take enough care

In the wee hours of the next morning
When they were still mourning
A monk was passing by
Seeing them grieve he asked the reason why

“We were ten, searching for bliss
But one of us we now miss
The river has probably taken him away
When the floods raged the previous day”

“All of you please stand in a line
And we shall see whether you’re ten or nine
I’ll give each one a tight slap
Just count the number when you hear the clap”

At the end of the last smack
All their joy was back
Up to ten they could count
Even as they did recount

To count himself, each one had omitted
This blunder all had committed
All then thanked the monk so wise
And asked for his advice

“O brave and curious men”
The monk said then
“When duties we count
Ourselves we fail to account

About others’ duties we always fret
And our own we conveniently forget
To our own when we stop being blind
Bliss then we are sure to find”

title: Who does the Gold Belong?
text:
There once was a king visionary
Of law he was the utmost luminary
Parikshet was his name
Far and wide was his fame

One evening to his court a dispute was brought
With a stirring question of law it was fraught
The plaintiff had bought the defendant’s land
Filled with just mud and sand

While digging, a pitcher the plaintiff had found
Full of gold it was buried under the ground
Now, the plaintiff had come to the court
With a definite purport

“This gold is something for which I did not pay
It must go back to the defendant without delay
This gold I wish to return
To fulfil my duty is all I yearn”

Back the defendant refused to take
Citing that his duty of conscience is at stake
“How can I accept the gold
Delivered from the womb of earth I had already sold”

When from their positions the parties won’t budge
The question became tough for the king to adjudge
“Come tomorrow at the first light”
And the wise king retired for the night

As the arguments resumed upon sunrise
The king was up for a big surprise
The plaintiff had changed his stand overnight
He was now arguing about his right

He now wanted to retain the gold
As the land included all things hidden in its fold
“Back all the gold I want to take
My right why should I forsake”

The defendant refuted, citing his own right
Armed with reason he too was ready to fight
“I had sold the land alone
Bereft of the treasure that lay hidden unknown”

We know not the dispute’s ultimate fate
It still remains a matter of legal debate
But the judicious king did proclaim
And asked his fellow men to listen with their wisdom aflame

“With ‘right’ when your brethren you want to defeat
When your ‘duty’ has taken the back seat
Then for sure the dark age of Kali is here to stay
Now truth, only the glitter of gold shall convey”

Of these twin elements, the whole law is an interplay
But can man take both together in his sway?
Indeed complementary they are
Bereft of duties rights cannot travel far

When we focus only on our right
Eternal strife we are bound to invite
When we also nurture our duty
For sure, we attain to truth, love and beauty

title: White Swans
text:
At dusk the king came to know
With joy he began to glow
He was in love with the white swan
And six were to arrive the following dawn

Of soldiers he had dispatched a team
To bring them from a faraway stream
As the swans were about to come
He wanted to give them a special welcome

In the royal garden a pond had been dug
And the final path was marked with the royal rug
But the king was not happy with all the décor
He wanted to do something more

It was already night
But the guests were so bright
And the king was so fond
So, with milk he decided to fill the pond

“But My Lord, How would we get so much amount
Of milk there is no readymade fount
In a few hours the swans would arrive
It seems impossible—howsoever we may strive”

“By all the people let milk be brought
We will ask everyone to bring just a small pot
For the whole country it is a moment of pride
So everybody would abide”

The duty was not so large
And everybody merrily agreed to discharge
The whole night
The masses cheerfully poured in the honour of swans bright

The excitement was so deep
The whole night the king could not sleep
And in the wee hours
The king stood out with flowers

At the first light
When the king was full of delight
And when the swans came near
White as milk they started to appear

But when towards the pond the king did walk
He was in for a big shock
Milk was nowhere to be seen
The pond was filled just with water clean

In the dead of night
In the absence of light
Water instead of milk, everyone had brought
Thinking that in the dark they will not be caught

Everyone thought “All others will perform their duty
And my water will not affect the pond’s beauty”
Maybe to the neighbour or to the brother
Why duty always belongs to the other

In the light we make promises huge
Then in darkness we hide and take refuge
But our duty if we miss
Then how can we attain to collective bliss

title: The Tale of Two Lakes
text:
Lakes two
Side by side they accrue
By the river Jordan both are fed
One full of life and the other called dead

The Sea of Galilee is ecstatic
Resplendent with life aquatic
Fish and frog merrily stay
Birds come, drink and fly away

The Sea of Galilee receives and then gives
That is why it lives
The river flows in and then moves out
Allowing all life to sprout

But nothing lives in the Dead Sea
With life it doesn’t agree
Bereft of vegetation
There is no chance of aquatic habitation

The Dead sea never flows out
Life there would only rout
When it would only hoard
With life how could it have any accord

Right without duty cannot live
Duty is when we give
Right is when we take
Let us not allow this cycle to break

A society cannot survive
If towards duty it does not strive
The importance of duty if we do not see
We are sure to end like the Dead Sea

title: The Glitter of Gold
text:
The glitter of gold
On our psyche has so much hold
We miss the diamond profound
And gold is nowhere to be found

Diamond we always had
But in mirage the gold was clad
Covered in shiny glaze
We begin an endless chase

The mirage we will never catch
We are sure to lose this match
For some time the glitter may amuse
But our diamond we may forever lose

Rights shine only at a distance
On their own they can have no existence
On other’s duty every right must stand
And in rights, others we seek to command

We can become truly wise
When our own duty we realise
Ourselves when we begin to direct
Real diamonds we are sure to collect

title: We—The Nation
text:
In the name of people all
Found the nation with our soul
Promise we made big and tall
Never shall we ever fall
Never fall
Never fall

Freedom is that we do cherish
Justice we shall never banish
Equal we are, not to blemish
Never shall we ever perish
Never perish
Never perish

Unity is that we must care
Wealth we must pool and share
Duty we must ever swear
WE will see then who can dare
Who can dare
Who can dare

title: Freedom of the Nation
text:
Gift it is certainly not
From the supermarket it cannot be bought
It’s a collective thought
And with action it is sought

Pride is its seed
Sweat its feed
To unity we must pay heed
And ever ready to bleed

It belongs to those who dare
But it’s a brittle affair
To preserve it requires upmost care
By our duty we must swear

title: Flow
text:
A new person when we meet
With attention we greet
Whatever we read
With that forever our mind we feed

We observe and find
And make an opinion about his nature and kind
Thereafter we close our mind
Forever the person is defined

A judgement we form
That becomes our norm
We presume and we deem
But consciousness is a stream

A person is not an object
On which life has no effect
Man is a continuum
And nature is a colosseum

In this universe vast
When change is the only law that would last
Nothing is constant always
There is nothing that forever stays

You can’t step into the same river twice
Change is nature’s binding devise
You can’t meet the same man again
Permanent opinions we must abstain

Every man is a flow
And every man has a chance to grow
Every saint has a past
And every sinner a future vast

title: Bow Down to Nature
text:
Earth is bleeding
Glaciers are receding
Birds are pleading
Slow down man

Rivers are dying
Ponds are drying
Fishes are crying
Look down man

Globe is warming
Air is warning
Bugs are swarming
Cool down man

Hills are falling
Hymns are calling
Laws are brawling
Clamp down man

Stars are not twinkling
Larks are not tinkling
You have no inkling
Bow down man

title: Trash to Treasure
text:
As our world turns into a violent bash
Where sounds blend and lights flash
Here old and new values clash
But in the end we collect only trash

The party will soon be over
Trash will be the only turnover
As a bleeding globe we hand over
Leaving future with a cruel hangover

Our planet urgently needs care
Everyone must be made aware
With posterity we must share
Enough of resources and clean air

Our fears how do we allay
Circular economy may be a way
Sustainability must forever stay
Trash must be the new cache

Greed always has an excuse
But Enough of abuse
We must learn to reduce
Recycle and reuse

We must not allow our planet to die
Our children won’t accept our alibi
‘Trash to treasure’ must become our war-cry
It’s a jingle we must codify

title: Happy Hill
text:
Jack and Jill
Went up the hill
To fetch a pail of water
On the hill so high
The spring was dry
As the Sun grew hot and hotter

The trees were crying
The grass was drying
And the flowers refused to bloom
The birds had gone
The bees had flown
And the hill was under a spell of gloom

Both came down
Striking their crown
As they told their sordid tale
No longer free
The neighbours did agree
Now water was up only for sale

The day is not far
When on water we shall spar
But we still have some time
Rain we must harvest
Every drop we must nest
And make wasting water a crime

For posterity we must leave
Enough they should receive
Ponds full and flowing springs
A happy hill
Is the best gift to will
With birds full of joy flying on their wings

title: Thief of the Sky
text:
Twinkle twinkle little star
Now I wonder where you are
Up above the world so high
But smoke is always in the sky

The night is bereft of all the glee
When the twinkle is so rare to see
Sad is the face of that little boy
Someone has robbed him of all his joy

But who has stolen the twinkling star
The thief is not so very far
We all have done the collective crime
Will we be forgiven by the time

Have we lost all our sanity
To have committed a crime against humanity
Now for a twinkle if we crave
The whole earth we need to save

Maybe there is still a chance
But all our actions we need to glance
The acts that are not environmentally benign
Must attract huge tax and fine

title: Friends Forever
text:
I was in search of glee
So I planted a tree
It grew and brought fresh air for free
Soon I heard the humming of a bee

Some birds would come and rest
Together they would chirp in jest
A few also built their nest
Glee was their only quest

Night and day
Nature’s play
I watch and pray
With glee I say

“We’ll be friends forever”

title: The Delicate Balance
text:
Man was a hunter and when he started to gather
Law and property were then born together
When was it? It’s not in my memory’s lather
We know it riding on imagination’s feather

When things were available in nature for free
They then belonged to the marauder’s spree
To avoid the disputes being decided by blood
The norm of ownership sprouted like a little bud

From movable to immovable the bud continued to grow
Things then belonged to the sweat of the brow
Man’s labour was the subject then to protect
To own more became a matter of respect

Limited were the things created with labour
But man wanted to own more than his neighbour
Intellectual creations were thus added to the list
Man then wanted to capture whole world in his fist

When ‘exclusive’ was the genre of all his right
Drunk he became with the wine of his might
Bothered he was not about the people’s plight
Who would then give the mighty a fight?

To transmute to order from such a chaos
‘Public interest’ soon came across
Though one is still permitted to own
But of sharing you cannot now be shorn

As the people’s lawyer laid bare this plea
It were the masses who shouted out with glee
But wait! Are we not approaching the same old spree?
Where things were set just for free

Public interest came as a gift to wonder
But even this can verily become a plunder
Is it in man’s destiny to go round and round?
And continue eternally with the same old wound?

Owning and sharing must go hand in hand
For expression, for invention and also for that famous brand
Striking this balance is like playing with glass
Delicate it remains even for the men of class

title: Progeny of Intellect
text:
I’m an idea nobody knew
Copying I eschew
You can definitely sue
If I’m not new

Ever since you were aboriginal
I’m Sometimes fictional
Sometimes mythical
But I’m always original

I was born as a spark
On an endless journey I want to embark
Make me your mark
And I’ll shine even in dark

Secret if you keep
And hide me deep
Many rewards you’ll reap
But don’t allow anyone to peep

Many treasures you’ll collect
If you treat me with respect
I may not be perfect
But I’m the progeny of your own intellect

I’m not peculiar to any race
I hate being confined to a limited space
I want to travel to every place
But throw me if I don’t have a human face

title: The Loop of New
text:
Laws in this group create property new
Though in subconscious we always knew
Water is old but fresh is the dew
In statutes and common law the rights do strew
Intellect is common and the binding glue

If your invention is new
And you’re first with the execution true
Something no one ever knew
The patent is sure to be through
The right then belongs only to you

Your expression need not be new
But it must originate surely from you
If only within you it grew
And from no one else you drew
Then copyright is yours—valid and true

Your mark should be older than its claimant new
By use in trade the rights do accrue
When a licensee uses, the rights still enure to you
Its value enhances if more people knew
If registered, don’t forget to renew

Maybe old or maybe new
It’s a secret no one ever knew
You need to keep it out of the view
But under promise you may share it too
And if someone steals, make sure to sue
An indication which cannot be new
Geographical link it must have true
Only an association can apply for the rights to endue
Licensing is something you must eschew
One of the last in this group to make its debut

Woods are fresh and pastures new
Pride in the owner it does endue
Great poise also it tends to imbue
Without it can survive only businesses few
Spectrum of market it shines ever through

title: Create Protect Innovate
text:
Create and innovate
Knowledge we generate
Fortune we date
With the world we relate

Protect and project
Never neglect
Ideas we respect
And the fruits of intellect

With pride we stand
And market we command
If we have in hand
New, original or that famous brand

Devote and promote
IP is the boat
For business to float
And high on the exchange to quote

Arise and awake
Eager to make
And to those who try to fake
Action we shall take

We own and we share
It’s a twin affair
Of duties aware
We also take care

title: An IP Wish
text:
With new passions
And new expressions
And new works to create
May with fortune you date

Let new ideas surge
And brilliant thoughts emerge
With new inventions
May you explore newer dimensions

May your good name
Find new fame
And your brands
Reach distant lands

May you come up with many a design
With new applications to mine
And your secrets to share
With new alliances to pair

May your new year be intellectually bright
With emergence of light
Let’s welcome twenty twenty-five
With renewed vigor to strive

title: The Promise
text:
I was born as a spark
On an endless journey I wish to embark
For a lasting bond I long
Goods and services I want to belong

On the wings of use
Profound and profuse
To the infinite sky
I wish to fly

I introduce the supplier
To the buyer
I make consumers aware
And trespassers beware

I promise to watch my owner’s interest
But for me consumers come first
About quality I do swear
Of buyer’s prestige I also take care

Ever vigilant and alert
I need to assert
Every fight that does not kill
Makes me stronger and takes me up that hill

On top of that hill I become well known
Universal then is my tone
I then belong to goods and services all
Markets and patrons I promise to enthrall

Whether physical or digital
For trade I am critical
My promise holds
As the virtual world unfolds

With future I can converse
I’ll see you in the metaverse
So, make me your mark
And I promise to shine even in dark

title: The Brittle Assets
text:
In our conscience deep
Secrets we all keep
We don’t want people to have any clue
But we also wish to share them with a few

Some secrets have personal tone
Others belong to the commercial zone
They can give a market edge
Provided we are able to hedge

In trade, secrets can take us far
But alas! brittle they are
Ever prone to theft
Dangerous may be the employees who have left

No protection against independent discovery
Once made public there is no recovery
If someone reverse engineers
Forever the secrecy disappears

The tool of patent is born
Only because secrets can be easily torn
Patent offers promises huge
Provided we come out of our secret’s refuge

But we want the best of both the domains
Together we want to walk in both the lanes
Patents we seek on some aspects
Secrets we want to keep in other respects

With such a mix
Markets we want to fix
We use patents as advertisements just
For our secrets to be conveyed in trust

title: Soul of Creativity
text:
Sometimes author is like a cloud
With his nectar all are equally endowed
The producer just needs to pick
And proceed with the flick

Sometimes author is like a stream
A faraway gleam
The producer must travel to his shore
And collect the gems as they pour

Sometimes author is like a well
Unknown in earth the pearls dwell
The producer must dig deep
And search for the seep

Varying may be author’s contribution and role
But of creativity he is the soul
Yet on the eve of film’s release
He is forgotten with ease

Obscured in small print
The payments often hint
To him law has not been fair
We need to take enough care

title: Man and Law
text:
When on the planet earth
Man for the first time took his birth
He was utterly inadequate and weak
But in one respect he was unique

Like other animals he could not run fast
In swimming competition he was amongst the last
Like birds he could not fly
Far could not see his eye

In climbing trees he was slower than most
About sense of smell too he could not boast
His teeth were not so sharp
Upon his claws he could hardly harp

Fire and tools were yet to be discovered
All the secrets of science were not yet uncovered
In this violent milieu how could he survive
How then could he remain alive

Because larger than others his group was sized
And certainly better organised
This was achieved with the sovereign’s command
Obedience of the whole group which could demand

This command of the sovereign man
Is nothing but the law of the human clan
With this superior law man could not only survive
But in this hostile environment he could also thrive

Many are the ways to generate
And for this command to emanate
One end of the spectrum is autocracy
And on the other lies democracy

title: Forest Trail
text:
Every forest trail
Tells an interesting tale
It can lead you to many a station
And maybe to some unknown destination

Why it never conforms to the straight line
Why it always forms a zigzag design
We can’t always decipher the reason
But someone has crafted it with precision

When man appeared on Earth
And announced his birth
These trails he found
Already marked on the ground

But these trails who made
No stone no plaque ever displayed
Numerous animals before man
Walked on these trails with their clan

Following animal footprints
Man always got hints
He then explored fresh woods and pastures new
But these trails always gave him the clue

On these trails man has now built roads
Superhighways carrying civilisational loads
But beneath the surface of a modern highway
An old trail would always lay

Are human customs not like a trail
Some inherent truth they always entail
Carried forward from the animal past
Wisdom of ages they have amassed

Customs of the yore
Their wisdom into legislations they always did pour
Whenever I scratched the surface of a modern law
The foundation of an old custom I always saw

title: Time and Law
text:
Law is temporal
To change is moral
Time tests every law
And finds its flaw

With time law must move
Only then in truth it will groove
If law makes friends with time
Only then with justice it will rhyme

Even a law embossed in sacred stone
By the winds of time is sure to be blown
Time and tide wait for none
With an obsolete law, justice can never be done

So make amends
Before its validity ends
The old remedy doesn’t heal
When the malady has a new zeal

In the hobo style
Stay only for a while
Always shift and roam
As they have no permanent home

Law is a constant endeavour
Can’t settle forever
For a while to perch
Then fly away in search

title: Hidden Potential
text:
Every letter is a hymn
No sound ever so dim
They can make a word
Which is sure to be heard

Every plant is a cure
Health it can ensure
Every poison is a nectar
It’s the quantity that would matter

Every heart has a treasure
Provided we care to measure
Every man is both friend and foe
One remains hidden while the other would show

Every saint has a past
Every man is so vast
Maybe down the slope
But every sinner has hope

Every danger gives a chance
For us to advance
Then why wait for the right time
When every moment is sublime
Law and Poetry; Legal Poetry; Poetry and Law

title: Happiness
text:
Boy O boy
I was in search of joy
So things I amassed
But the pleasure didn’t last

In search of thrill
I scaled the summit of that distant hill
It was not worth the trouble
Fleeting it was like a soap-bubble

In search of bliss
Pride I didn’t miss
But the coin was fake
Like a bitter cake

Got everything I desired
But my feet got tired
When I could no longer move forward
I turned inward

In friendship I found glee
In gratitude I could see
In creativity it flows
In prayer it grows

title: The Mysterious Law
text:
Wherever you go, you carry
Around the world its style would never vary
Its central theme is the same
Even the most powerful it could tame

With it, if you make friends
There will be no need to make amends
Never would you ever repent
People are ready to give consent

It’s the key
To unlock the veiled plea
Doors would open even when previously closed
Agreeable they become even when opposed

The fake one would wither away
For long it cannot stay
With it, peace begins
And comity ever wins

When you apply
Others also tend to comply
It is self-propagating
Its effect is never abating

The hidden teeth would appear
If you examine from near
With it you become lighter
And the world becomes brighter

Freely you may share
Without caution or care
You may pass it on even to strangers
But it becomes difficult to keep it in dangers

The world it can transform and change
Long is its range
Its curve can set things straight
Its effect is great

It is something that even ancient humans had
It can also make animals glad
It’s the antique way
From troubles to get away

In every situation it can fit
It should be in every man’s tool kit
Its effect is quick and fast
But forever it may last

In light everyone can surely see
Even in darkness it can give glee
There is no need to abridge
It can make even the most difficult bridge

It’s no secret to keep
Its reach is far and deep
Oh, I was not talking about law in poetic style
I was just referring to the power of a smile

title: Survival
text:
In the backside of our home
A cat started living under the junkyard dome
Soon she gave birth to kittens three
We all were now full of glee

Every morning she would go to hunt
A squirrel or a rat she must confront
She would nurse the kids with great devotion
A bowl of milk was the contribution of our emotion

The first kitten was very fast and nimble
Of speed he was the ultimate symbol
The second was also agile
But the third one was too fragile

The first two would quickly approach the bowl
And would like to drink it all
With anger the mother would growl and pique
Milk for the third one if they did not keep

The first two quickly learnt to walk and climb
But the third one took so much more time
He was slow in every respect
Energy he could just not collect

We were sure he would not survive
But with great love the mother continued to strive
She would patiently teach and wait
The slow one’s life was not left to fate

Independent the two kittens quickly grew
Now they ventured to explore paths ever new
But the slow guy used to always cling
With the mother he was tied with an invisible string

One day the first kitten ventured out all alone
A speeding car—and he was dead and gone
A few days later the second one climbed the wall
Till the next street he continued to crawl

He was playing very smart
But still the dogs there ripped him apart
Now only the slow and shy remained
Eventually in the game of life only he sustained

Gradually he learnt the tricks of life
And continued till the end of his strife
He was destined to take it ahead
Through him her genes would now spread

‘Survival of the fittest’ may have some flaw
‘Survival of the dearest’ is certainly a competing law
Nature is immense and vast
It is yet to reveal the law that is last

title: Marriage and Divorce
text:
Scriptures eulogise it as a sacrament
A union with lifelong commitment
To enter one was free
But there was no out-door to flee

For the whole life to each other they must belong
Through the vagaries of times together they have to move along
This good law lasted for long
Only in the modern times we found it to be wrong

“What if things don’t go as per my plan
Why should then I suffer for the full life span
When the other is hell
Then together why should I dwell

So, give me a slit to slip out”
Law said, “To what you propose though I have my doubt
Yet take it if you insist; but out before you move
The other’s guilt you must prove”

Then there was a demand to make it free of proof and debate
“Why should law approve when we have decided to separate”
Law then agreed to introduce divorce by consent
With just a role of recordation the court must then be content

Soon people will say “why wait for other’s consent
When notice of divorce I have already sent
I have spoken divorce
So, my marriage is no longer in force”

For marriage indeed you need two
But for divorce just one would do
When this circle is complete
Would marriage itself not become obsolete?

Why give it a form
When just to live-in becomes the new norm
You are free to move in and out
And also to wander about

Liberation from bondage we will indeed attain
But with that the institution of marriage goes down the drain
Without divorce for millennia the society did thrive
With divorce for how long would it survive?

title: The Other
text:
On the edge of a small town
Under a tree an old man sat down
With life’s chores he was done
Now he cherished the company of air and Sun

As the old man basked
A rider stopped by and asked
“Are the people of this town good and kind”
“But why do you want to find”

“Am looking for a place to settle down
As I have left a town
Where people are very bad and lack all grace
So, desperately I look for a new place ”

“Brother, you better move on
For people of this town are masters of con
They are wicked and vile
Treachery is their only style”

As the rider moved on to depart
Another man arrived on his bullock cart
He also expressed a desire to settle down
And enquired about the character of the town

“Son, how about people of the village you dwelled?”
Up with tears the traveller’s eyes welled
“People there are loving and nice
They live happily without a single vice

I look for a place here for economic reason
But I will remember those people in every season”
“Son, you are welcome
Here people are more loving than from where you come”

A young boy listened to all this
With surprise he was amiss
“Grandfather, why opposite things did you say
To two persons in a single day”

“The other is hell
If in your heart, hate you allow to dwell
Like heaven the other would appear
If with love your heart you steer

Whatever you perceive
The universe will achieve
Whatever you send forth comes back manifold
Life is an echo” the old man told

title: Friendship's Domain
text:
Friendship is no barter
And it has no charter
The bond is not a contract
But from it you never retract

It is not a venture
Rather an adventure
A perilous sea you need to cross
Where your ego must go for a toss

It belongs to those who are ready to gamble
For wager is its very preamble
The grand risk you must take
Your life must be put at stake

Out of the window when all doubt would go
Cool breeze of trust would come in a lavish flow
The palace is full of wonder
But it’s trove you cannot plunder

What a challenge it is to be a friend
The barrier of envy you need to transcend
If you try to pretend
It will soon come to a bitter end

Siblings are ordinary; marriage is profane
And all relationships just go in vain
Unless you arrive at that sweet plane
Which is called friendship’s domain

Laden with conditions, it’s not a pact
With divine mystery it is always stacked
In friendship life knows that celestial thrill
Where you can drink to your heart’s fill

It’s a journey where on each step you find a treasure
And joy you grab without a measure
In the company of friend you can drop all your armour
Life is then blissful and the bond so much warmer

title: Law and Love
text:
For some law is propelled by fear
In the right direction it makes them steer
For them lady law won’t be dear
If that sword she does not bear

To some law is a bargain
Something they are prepared to lose for something to gain
Pleasure they exchange for pain
Duty they perform for rights to obtain

Some are wise
To see through they have the eyes
That bereft of law the boat of life would capsize
So, law for them is a necessary device

A charming dove
Majestically hovering above
No need for fear, bargain or wisdom to shove
Is there anyone for whom law is just love?

title: The Song of Shri Raam
text:
The Song of Raam

The prince was charming
But the demons were swarming
The task was huge
And jungle the only refuge

For the sake of his bride
And for his clan’s pride
To create an order just
War was then a must

His jungle army marched
Bows were then arched
When the ocean saw its guilt
A path was then built

His envoy did thunder
And called for surrender
But the enemy chose fight
Now it was the test of might

He fought like a gale
His weapon must not fail
The fort was busted
The enemy was dusted

In that victory so grand
Spoils of war he banned
Back from his jungle camp
In memory we light a lamp

title: Two Blind Girls
text:
A long long while ago
When time had just begun to flow
Two girls were born
By the sense of sight, both were forlorn

Blinded at birth
They search for their worth
One focuses on duty
The other on beauty

One is blind of emotions
The other is blinded by emotions
One perceives the world by reason
For the other it remains forbidden as treason

One is aloof from whoever comes in front
Whether with rich or poor she does confront
The other can feel only when one comes near
To her the rest of the world just doesn’t appear

One always pursues what is fair
The only guide in her every affair
For the other everything is fair
At all costs she wants to share

One likes to weigh
Scales always show her the way
The other uses only her heart
All knowledge to her, it does impart

If either of them smiled at you
Heaven you immediately knew
And if any one of them does frown
In a pool of pity, you are sure to drown

Blindness they ever embrace
And only in blindness they find their grace
Into law the first girl eventually transformed
The other became love when to blindness she conformed
